scores.evidence: Dedup... RocksDB state store in Flink with a TTL... gives exactly-once *effect* even though delivery is at-least-once.
scores.rationale: Technical claims are accurate and precise throughout, including subtle areas (gapless invoice sequences vs DB sequences, SAQ-A scoping, Kafka partition ordering, RLS mechanics, double-entry invariants) with real limits stated honestly.

scores.evidence: This design targets **(A)** because it covers (B) as well... Some of those answers could remove large parts of this design.
scores.rationale: Resolves the request's central ambiguity explicitly, enumerates the core billing capabilities, sequences delivery into a realistic phased MVP, and justifies what could be removed under narrower interpretations.

scores.evidence: The ledger is the source of truth for money. All other money data is either derived from it or a document that points to ledger entries.
scores.rationale: Guiding principles (immutability, pure rating, explicit time, idempotency) are honored consistently in every flow — late events go to the next invoice, entitlements never query invoices, outbox ties events to transactions.

scores.evidence: Chaos tests that kill workers mid-workflow and inject PSP timeouts, then assert the invariants still hold.
scores.rationale: Validation is built around the domain's actual failure risks — test clocks, property-based proration tests, golden invoice fixtures, shadow billing before cutover, and continuously-monitored ledger invariants that page in production.

scores.evidence: To tailor this further, the most useful details would be: which of (A) or (B)... Some of those answers could remove large parts of this design.
scores.rationale: Scope and scale assumptions are stated up front, the interpretation choice is explicit, and the plan says which answers would change the design and how (removing metering pipeline or cells).

scores.evidence: PSP timeout ("did it charge?") — Idempotency key on retry. Query the PSP before re-attempting. Webhooks plus reconciliation settle the truth
scores.rationale: Major billing failure modes (duplicates, partial workflow failures, aggregator lag, tax outage, cross-tenant leaks) get concrete handling, but chargebacks/disputes and forged inbound PSP webhooks (no signature verification) are missing.

scores.evidence: Invariants to monitor continuously, with pages on violation: Ledger debits equal credits.
scores.rationale: Domain-meaningful health signals, reconciliation jobs, replay UI, audited support access and safe-change mechanisms (shadow billing, draft windows) are strong, but code deployment/rollback, schema migrations and incident ownership are not addressed.

scores.evidence: MVP (one cell, about 3 to 4 months, small team)
scores.rationale: Beyond a rough MVP effort estimate and a 'cheap' label on S3, there is no analysis of run-cost drivers, how costs grow with event volume, vendor fees, or cost controls for the heavy streaming stack.

scores.evidence: Decisions to make early (they're expensive to change later)... Ledger-first design. Retrofitting double-entry later is very painful.
scores.rationale: One-way decisions (merchant of record, ledger, immutable price versions, money representation, tenant-cell routing) are explicitly isolated and front-loaded, while vendor coupling is abstracted behind PSP/tax adapters with stated alternatives.

scores.evidence: Why not database-per-tenant by default? At 10k tenants it makes migrations, connection pooling and cross-tenant operations painful.
scores.rationale: Every heavyweight component is justified against stated scale/scope, the MVP starts with one cell and one PSP, and the plan itself flags which parts (metering pipeline, cells) can be dropped if assumptions narrow.

scores.evidence: Idempotency. Invoice creation is keyed by (subscription_id, period_start, period_end) with a unique constraint, so a retried workflow can't double-bill.
scores.rationale: Decisions are implementation-specific (schemas, partition keys, state machines, API sketch), the phased order follows real dependencies (ledger and catalog before usage billing), and CI golden fixtures and invariants provide checkable intermediate results.

checklist.evidence: Store amounts as BIGINT minor units plus an ISO currency code... Round once, at the line-item level... Never use floats.
Finalized financial documents never change. Corrections are made with credit notes and adjustments, never by updating rows.
Every PSP call carries an idempotency key derived from (invoice_id, attempt_no)... dedupe by PSP event ID and process asynchronously.
Card data never touches your servers. Use PSP-hosted fields or Elements so you stay at SAQ-A, and store only PSP tokens.
RLS plus tenant-scoped repositories in code, plus automated tests that try cross-tenant access on every endpoint
Events that arrive after finalization go onto the next invoice as a dated adjustment line. The finalized invoice is never touched.
A PriceVersion is immutable... Subscriptions point to a specific version... Plan changes are stored as SubscriptionPhases with effective timestamps.
Handle VAT/GST reverse charge, tax-exempt customers (with certificates stored)... Many jurisdictions require gapless sequences per tenant.
Retries are scheduled sensibly (for example days 1, 3, 5 and 7... card-updater support and escalating email sequences.
A nightly reconciliation job compares ledger and payments against PSP settlement reports and raises alerts on any mismatch.
Product code calls it, with local caching and short TTLs, and never queries invoices. This decouples product availability from billing outages.
In case (B), also look hard at buying (Stripe Billing, Orb, Metronome, Chargebee) and building only entitlements and metering.

traps.evidence: Store amounts as BIGINT minor units plus an ISO currency code... Never use floats.
Append-only: no UPDATE or DELETE grants on this table... corrected with a credit note that references specific lines.
Store raw payloads, dedupe by PSP event ID and process asynchronously... Idempotency key on retry. Query the PSP before re-attempting.
Card data never touches your servers... store only PSP tokens.
Postgres Row-Level Security (SET app.tenant_id per transaction)... automated tests that try cross-tenant access on every endpoint

note: An expert-grade billing architecture that avoids every classic trap with precise, consistent mechanisms; its only real weaknesses are absent cost reasoning, missing dispute/chargeback and inbound webhook-signature handling, and thin deployment/ownership detail.
